\chapter{Offers, Apologies, Introductions}
\label{ch:te-offers-apologies}
\hlchaptermodality{94}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can beg pardon, apologise, offer something, decline politely, and say I am glad of an introduction.}

Complete TE-C94-introduction: the courtesies around a first visit.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[manniñcaṇḍi]{\te{మన్నించండి} (manniñcaṇḍi) — please pardon me}

\label{lesson:TE-C94-pardon}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for gladly, then the Telugu for the body.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{మన్నించండి}}
\textbf{\te{మన్నించండి}} (\emph{manniñcaṇḍi}) — \textquotedblleft{}please pardon me\textquotedblright{}.

It does the work of \textbf{\te{క్షమించండి}}, and is the gentler, native word beside it. Either answers a mistake; \textbf{\te{మన్నించండి}} is the one to use with an elder.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A second apology, softer than the first.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{manniñcaṇḍi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{manniñcaṇḍi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{manniñcaṇḍi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for gladly, then the Telugu for the body, then say \emph{manniñcaṇḍi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{మన్నించండి} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Please pardon me\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kṣamāpaṇa]{\te{క్షమాపణ} (kṣamāpaṇa) — an apology}

\label{lesson:TE-C94-apology}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for the body, then the Telugu for pardon me.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{క్షమాపణ}}
\textbf{\te{క్షమాపణ}} (\emph{kṣamāpaṇa}) — \textquotedblleft{}an apology\textquotedblright{}, the noun.

\textbf{\te{క్షమాపణ} \te{చెప్పండి}} — \textquotedblleft{}say sorry\textquotedblright{}. It comes from the same root as \textbf{\te{క్షమించండి}}: to forgive, and to ask forgiveness.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The apology as a thing you can give.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kṣamāpaṇa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kṣamāpaṇa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kṣamāpaṇa ceppaṇḍi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for the body, then the Telugu for pardon me, then say \emph{kṣamāpaṇa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{క్షమాపణ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An apology\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kāvālā?]{\te{కావాలా}? (kāvālā?) — do you want it?}

\label{lesson:TE-C94-offer}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for pardon me, then the Telugu for an apology.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{కావాలా}?}
\textbf{\te{కావాలా}?} (\emph{kāvālā?}) — \textquotedblleft{}do you want it?\textquotedblright{}.

It is \textbf{\te{కావాలి}}, \textquotedblleft{}is wanted\textquotedblright{}, with the question \textbf{-\te{ఆ}}. \textbf{\te{టీ} \te{కావాలా}?} — \textquotedblleft{}would you like tea?\textquotedblright{}. The answer is \textbf{\te{కావాలి}} or \textbf{\te{వద్దు}}, both yours already.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An offer, and both of its answers.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāvālā?}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāvālā?}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} ask \emph{ṭī kāvālā?}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for pardon me, then the Telugu for an apology, then say \emph{kāvālā?} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{కావాలా}? mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Do you want it?\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[avasaraṁ]{\te{అవసరం} (avasaraṁ) — need, necessity}

\label{lesson:TE-C94-need}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for an apology, then the Telugu for do you want it.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{అవసరం}}
\textbf{\te{అవసరం}} (\emph{avasaraṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}need\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{అవసరం} \te{లేదు}} — \textquotedblleft{}there is no need\textquotedblright{}, the polite way to refuse help, with the \textbf{\te{లేదు}} of your first chapter.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A way to refuse kindly.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avasaraṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avasaraṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{avasaraṁ lēdu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for an apology, then the Telugu for do you want it, then say \emph{avasaraṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{అవసరం} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Need, necessity\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[paricayaṁ]{\te{పరిచయం} (paricayaṁ) — an introduction, acquaintance}

\label{lesson:TE-C94-introduction}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for do you want it, then the Telugu for need.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{పరిచయం}}
\textbf{\te{పరిచయం}} (\emph{paricayaṁ}) — \textquotedblleft{}an introduction, an acquaintance\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\te{మీతో} \te{పరిచయం} \te{సంతోషం}} — \textquotedblleft{}glad to have met you\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}the acquaintance with you is a joy\textquotedblright{}. A fuller form of the \textbf{\te{సంతోషం}} you said at your first meeting.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Pardon, an apology, an offer, a refusal, and a fuller pleased-to-meet-you.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paricayaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{paricayaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mītō paricayaṁ santōṣaṁ}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for do you want it, then the Telugu for need, then say \emph{paricayaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{పరిచయం} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An introduction, acquaintance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
